findings.issue: The colon after su ofrenda presents Najshón as the offering. אֶת marks קָרְבָּנוֹ as object of the hiphil participle הַמַּקְרִיב; the proper name identifies that offerer.
acercante can be read as merely drawing near; the participle is hiphil (bring something near).

notes: Judá is the locked form; Najshón and Aminadav have no lock in the packet.
